answer: A pigment-dyed jetty terrace mooring pass keeps fakes off the docks. First, each newcomer stakes 180 POA and registers an 80-dollar hardware key, then does six supervised moorings along the jetty, each signed by a different harbormaster. Second, harbormasters inspect the cargo before dyeing the pass with an uncopyable pigment mark. Third, a failed audit burns the stake and bans the key for 180 days. Forging 1,000 passes would cost 180,000 POA, 80,000 dollars, and 6,000 staged moorings. Like a harbor that trusts only boats it has watched tie up, the terrace stays open to the honest.
